one_line: A human-governed WebMCP co-DM for shared text adventures.

leverage_rationale: Typed scene, lore, entity, messaging, and approval-gated mutation tools create shared state and accountability that UI-driving automation would handle less reliably.
leverage_evidence: ABOUT describes five registered browser-native tools and server authorization/audit receipts.
ABOUT explicitly keeps high-impact changes queued for human approval.
execution_rationale: The packet presents a coherent game/DM console concept, but visual evidence is mostly a dark technical workspace and no end-to-end gameplay proof or transcript is supplied.
execution_evidence: Three frame sheets show a persistent split-pane technical workspace and later console/log state.
Devpost ABOUT describes real-time DM and player views but the packet has no video transcript.
impact_rationale: Tabletop groups and DMs have a concrete need for shared lore, state management, and safe assistance; the approval model fits consequential game-master actions.
impact_evidence: Pitch targets tabletop campaigns and shared players/DMs.

creativity_rationale: The co-DM framing and accountable proposal workflow are a fresh synthesis of text adventure, campaign tooling, and WebMCP.

one_line: A local-first registry that turns reviewed site action packs into governed WebMCP tools.
what_it_does: Binds manifests to exact origins/fingerprints, exposes typed tools in signed-in sessions, projects bounded untrusted output, and requires human authorization for writes.
leverage_rationale: The product directly addresses how agents gain reliable, typed capabilities in existing authenticated sites, with drift detection and governance unavailable to ordinary UI automation.
leverage_evidence: ABOUT describes reviewed action packs compiled into live tools in the user's signed-in session.
ABOUT specifies exact-origin binding, fail-closed drift, bounded output, and human authority on consequences.
execution_rationale: The architecture and safety model are unusually coherent, but the packet lacks a submitted video and the visual sheet is technical rather than a clearly demonstrated end-to-end workflow.
execution_evidence: ABOUT gives concrete runtime, manifest, origin, output, and approval behavior.
Frame sheets show a stable technical dashboard and console/log states.
impact_rationale: Operations teams using portals without APIs are a specific, broad problem; the proposed adoption path is credible and directly addresses agent access and safety.
impact_evidence: ABOUT identifies Grafana, Cal.com, payer portals, vendor consoles, and admin dashboards as targets.
Public repository and live demo are reported in FACTS.
creativity_rationale: Reframing WebMCP adoption around user-owned reviewed packs rather than vendor implementation is highly original and ambitious.
creativity_evidence: The packet's central inversion is one user/one tab/one reviewed pack at a time.
Declarative, non-executable manifests and fail-closed drift are a distinctive interaction model.
usability_note: The governance model is clear conceptually; actual setup and pack authoring friction are not demonstrated.
red_flags: No submitted video/transcript; claims of measured coverage are not independently demonstrated in packet.
standouts: Strong safety posture: origin binding, bounded output, human authorization.
WebMCP is central rather than decorative.
advance_reason: Exceptional WebMCP leverage and a compelling infrastructure thesis; execution should be verified in a later stage.

one_line: A human-owned archive that grants agents fine-grained access to curated taste and context.
what_it_does: Organizes visual references and work, compiles folder/region permissions into the agent's WebMCP tool surface, and supports feedback-driven creative workbenches.
leverage_rationale: Dynamic permission-scoped tool registration makes agent access reflect human grants and shared live archive state; general UI automation cannot match this cleanly.
leverage_evidence: ABOUT says grants compile into tool surfaces and schemas, narrow grants re-register, and revocation removes tools.
Transcript describes Codex using curated taste to create and upload a landing page.
execution_rationale: The video transcript provides a coherent archive-to-agent-to-workbench flow, while the packet describes concrete permission and feedback states.
execution_evidence: 178-second video is reported with transcript covering archive, agent access, generated workbench, and feedback.
ABOUT describes visual workspace, folder grants, and contribution/edit permissions.
impact_rationale: Designers and creative professionals have a real problem managing reference context and taste; visible ownership and correction can improve repeated agent work.
impact_evidence: ABOUT identifies images, links, documents, notes, prior work, and task-specific agent access.
Transcript shows a generated landing page shaped by archived taste.
creativity_rationale: Treating taste as a curated, permissioned, feedback-bearing agent resource is a memorable and ambitious interaction model.
creativity_evidence: The concept separates human-owned archive/taste from opaque agent memory.
Dynamic tool/schema changes based on folder grants are novel product behavior.
usability_note: The archive/workbench framing is understandable and the transcript indicates a practical creative loop.
red_flags: Some claims are transcript-described rather than independently inspectable here.
standouts: Fine-grained permission compilation into WebMCP tools.
Taste curation plus explicit positive/negative feedback.
advance_reason: Strong evidence-backed concept with unusually deep human-agent context control.

one_line: A fertility journey workspace with agent-assisted matching and human-controlled introductions.
what_it_does: Reads journey status, filters authorized donor/surrogate profiles, opens permitted details, and prepares—but does not submit—introductions.
leverage_rationale: Page-defined tools keep the agent grounded in the user's live journey and authorized candidate view, while preserving a consequential human final action.
leverage_evidence: ABOUT lists journey, timeline, candidate search/open, and prepare-introduction tools.

advance_reason: High-impact, well-scoped use case with credible WebMCP grounding; verify execution later.

one_line: A storefront where agent purchases are governed by standing rules and tamper-evident receipts.
what_it_does: Lets agents search/cart/checkout through WebMCP while humans approve thresholded purchases, inspect hash-chained receipts, cancel, and refund.
leverage_rationale: Human-gated pending tool calls, abort handling, policy citations, and shared receipt state are capabilities ordinary browser clicking cannot provide reliably.
leverage_evidence: ABOUT describes request_checkout pausing for approval and returning pending_approval with receipt id.
ABOUT says get_recent_receipts exposes the same hash-chained trail to agent and human.
execution_rationale: The product contract is detailed and coherent, but there is no video and only one gallery image, so actual checkout completion is not sufficiently evidenced.
execution_evidence: ABOUT specifies checkout, approval, abort, receipts, standing rules, and refunds.
FACTS reports live demo and public repo but no submitted video.
impact_rationale: Trustworthy delegation of purchases addresses a clear agent-commerce barrier and gives shoppers understandable control and accountability.
impact_evidence: Pitch targets shoppers delegating real storefront purchases.
Standing rules and one-tap approval/undo directly address money-risk concerns.
creativity_rationale: The receipt trail as a first-class bidirectional agent-human governance surface is a strong, memorable extension of commerce checkout.
creativity_evidence: Tamper-evident receipts, policy citations, pending calls, and abort semantics are integrated into the purchase model.
usability_note: The policy and receipt concepts are legible; real checkout interaction is not shown.
red_flags: Very thin visual evidence: one gallery image and no video.
Claims of tamper evidence and refunds are not independently verified in packet.
standouts: Approval that can suspend a tool call mid-execution.
Shared receipt trail with standing-rule citations.
advance_reason: Potentially transformative trust layer, but execution evidence is thin.

one_line: DrawMCP puts typed WebMCP tools directly on a shared Excalidraw canvas.
what_it_does: Lets agents summarize, select, add, update, delete, fit, and organize elements in the same live canvas with revision-aware writes.
leverage_rationale: Shared live canvas state, revision checks, cancellation, and one undo history materially outperform a remote MCP canvas or DOM-driving agent.
leverage_evidence: ABOUT lists seven canvas tools and a single human/agent revision history.
ABOUT claims expected_revision, serialized competing changes, validation, and cancellation.
execution_rationale: The scope is concrete and implementation details are coherent, but frame sheets rather than a video make end-to-end demonstrated behavior incomplete.
execution_evidence: ABOUT describes React/TypeScript/Vite and published Excalidraw SDK integration.
FACTS report live demo and public repository.
impact_rationale: Developers and teams routinely need architecture diagrams; eliminating the second-canvas/export reconciliation problem provides clear value.
impact_evidence: ABOUT describes human sketching plus agent continuation on the same canvas.
Side-by-side comparison with official Excalidraw MCP targets a concrete workflow boundary.
creativity_rationale: The shared-canvas and revision-aware WebMCP interaction is a strong, focused synthesis rather than a generic drawing wrapper.
creativity_evidence: Single source of truth and expected revision are central to the concept.
usability_note: Familiar Excalidraw surface plus structured agent actions should be approachable; live behavior is not fully shown.
red_flags: No submitted video/transcript; measured performance claim is not independently evidenced in packet.
advance_reason: Strong WebMCP delta and focused creative/developer utility.

leverage_rationale: Automated conversion from arbitrary page actions to agent tools could remove the site-by-site implementation bottleneck, though heuristic DOM discovery may be less reliable than authored tools.
leverage_evidence: ABOUT describes MV3 extension and agent skill discovering forms/actions and registering tools.
